newsitem.title: CANADA: Alberta Wheat Pool estimates grain/oilseed grades.
newsitem.headline: Alberta Wheat Pool estimates grain/oilseed grades.

text.p: Alberta Wheat Pool on Friday estimated quality levels of its grain and oilseed harvest, with 46 percent of crops combined by Sept 20.
AWP downgraded quality from last week's estimate because of wet weather conditions. Ten stations reported light frost damage.
Forty percent of hard red spring wheat should grade No1 Canada Western Red Spring, compared to 29 percent in the 10 year average.
Twenty eight percent of spring wheat should grade No2 CWRS compared to 24 percent in the past 10 years.
Twenty four percent of spring wheat should grade No3 CWRS versus 30 percent in the 10 year average and eight percent should grade as feed wheat, compared to 16 percent.
Twenty percent of barley should grade as malt compared to 13 percent in the last 10 years.
Sixty nine percent of barley should grade as No1 Canada Western feed compared to 71 percent over the past 10 years, 11 percent should grade as No2 CW compared to 16 percent.
Seventy seven percent of canola should grade as No1 Canada compared to 72 percent in the past 10 years, 18 percent should grade No2 C versus 17 percent.
Four percent of canola should grade No3 C compared to seven percent in the past 10 years and one percent should grade as Sample compared to three percent.
